Subject: Draft MSA redlines + security ask (SOC 2 + pentest access)

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for the call this morning. Attached are our initial redlines to the MSA and the Order Form. Two security-specific asks we need captured in the contract before legal can approve:

1) Explicit SOC 2 Type II report delivery cadence (we prefer annual delivery + summary of scope).
2) A defined pen-test access window per year with a minimal 10 business day notice and a list of staging IPs/contacts.

Also included is a short spreadsheet that maps our evidence requests to SOC2 categories (control families) — you can see the items we flagged as "high priority".

Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
- Provide a SOC 2 summary and encrypted artifact (PDF) for the prior 12 months;
- Commit to a pen-test scheduling window and agree to a lightweight evidence cadence (quarterly or ad-hoc) we can operationalize;
- Add language on data retention and audit logs retention to the exhibit.

Attachments: MSA_redlines_040328.docx (docx), Security_Exhibit_Proposal_040328.xlsx (xlsx)

Happy to jump on a short sync if helpful. We are targetting internal sign-off by Apr 12.

Best,
Julia

ClearRiver Health

Subject: RE: Fwd: Draft MSA redlines + security ask (SOC 2 + pentest access)

Kimberly —

Thanks for the heads up. Quick notes after an initial pass on the attachments:

1) SOC 2 delivery cadence: we can agree to provide the SOC 2 Type II report on an annual basis (encrypted PDF delivered within 30 days of availability) and a 1-page control-scope summary on request. We should avoid committing to continuous access or on-demand audit unless customer signs a deeper inspection addendum. Proposed clause: "Customer may request Provider's most recent SOC 2 Type II report and a binding summary of scope; Provider will deliver the encrypted artifact within 30 days of request. Further audit rights require a mutually agreed inspection addendum."

2) Pen-test access: Ben, can you confirm runbook. My position: we offer a single annual pen-test window per customer (2 weeks) plus a limited ad-hoc remediation verification check (1-2 days) with 10 business days' notice for non-emergency tests. We should avoid open-ended multi-window commitments.

3) Evidence cadence: propose mapping to three buckets — scheduled (annual SOC artifacts), quarterly operational summaries (token and latency metrics, no PII), and ad-hoc evidentiary requests that must follow the evidence guide and be scoped to the exhibit.

Laura — I'm attaching inline edits to the MSA redlines docx (see attachment MSA_redlines_040328-priyom-edits.docx). If legal accepts, we can propose those back to ClearRiver and offer an ops beat: option A (single 2-week window annually) or option B (one 1-week window + one limited verification).

I'll draft suggested contract language by EOD.

-priyom
From: Eli Turner <eli.turner@clearriverhealth.com>

Subject: Re: Draft MSA redlines + security ask (SOC 2 + pentest access)

Kimberly / Priyom —

Thanks for the quick reply and helpful options. The team discussed and prefers Option A (single 2-week annual window). A few clarifying points for the clause we will take to our legal:

- Please include a requirement to provide a point-of-contact who will be available during the pen-test window and provide staging IP addresses at least 5 business days prior.
- For SOC 2 delivery: annual encrypted report is acceptable; we'd like the 1-page control-scope summary included as an exhibit rather than 'on request' if that's acceptable.
- Evidence cadence: quarterly operational summaries are great — we only need high-level metrics (uptime, token volumes, major incidents) not logs.

We can accept the inspection addendum approach if it is limited to scenarios where we need deeper forensic access (incident-driven or regulatory). Please send proposed contract text and we'll fast-track our internal sign-off.

Attachments: SOC2-snapshot-2027.pdf (for your reference; this is our preferred format).

Eli
Sr. InfoSec, ClearRiver Health

Subject: RE: Draft MSA redlines + security ask (SOC 2 + pentest access)

Julia / Eli —

Appreciate the clarity and for providing the SOC sample. We've prepared contract language that preserves Redwood's limited-inspection posture while meeting your operational asks. Key points in the proposed exhibit:

• SOC2 Delivery: "Provider will deliver its most recent SOC 2 Type II report in encrypted PDF form within 30 days of availability; a one-page scope summary will be attached as Exhibit A to the Security Exhibit."

• Pen-test Window: "Provider will offer one annual Penetration Test Window (up to 10 business days of testing activity) or two-week window at Customer's election; Provider will require minimum ten (10) business days' advance notice and will provide a single technical point-of-contact and staging IPs at least five (5) business days before the start of the window. Ad-hoc remediation verification checks (no more than two business days) are allowed with five (5) business days' notice and do not require a separate visit."

• Evidence Cadence: "Provider will provide quarterly operational summaries restricted to high-level metrics (uptime, token volume trends, summary of material incidents) and will not disclose PII or raw logs absent a separate inspection addendum."

• Inspection Addendum: we've included a short addendum template for forensic or regulator-driven inspections that requires mutual agreement on scope, duration, and compensable time.

Please see attached: MSA_redlines_040328-laura-final.docx and Security_Exhibit_Proposal_040328.xlsx (updated). If that language looks good, Kimberly will share a redlined MSA with DocuSign and we can request your internal legal to review.

Next steps I propose:
- Julia/Eli: confirm acceptance of the language above by Mon Apr 9 so we can circulate the redline.
- If accepted, Kimberly will send the DocuSign packet and ask for signature on the Order Form to lock the pen-test slot window for calendar Q3.

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
